# PR #2970: Patch: Extended art, Pixel and Comic card versions

Closes #2942

This adds the three Epic versions from part 3 of #2725: **Extended art**, **Pixel** and **Comic**. Each is offered on its own seeded share of cards, and every check I ran passed; a component screenshot shows the looks on a Unit and a Spell, base and Radiant. I followed the plan, with seven departures listed under Decisions.

## What changed

**Server**
- `cosmetics.json` gains `version-extended-art`, `version-pixel` and `version-comic`. All are Epic, so none is a chase, and none is a default or a starter.
- Every offer clause samples by the version's own id:
  - **Extended art**: 40% of Spells and Field Spells, plus 40% of Legendary and Mythic cards. 156 cards; Training Grounds is lowest at 9.
  - **Pixel**: 40% of Rare and Epic Units, Traps and Field Traps, plus 40% of Legendary and Mythic cards. 95 cards; Meditative+ is lowest at 4.
  - **Comic**: 35% of Rare and Epic Units, Spells and Traps, plus 40% of Legendary and Mythic cards. 138 cards; Meditative+ is lowest at 5.
- I got these counts from the server's sample, recomputed independently; they match the plan's.
- No migration is needed: `seed-catalog` upserts registry entries.
- `cosmetics.rs` adds the three ids and the `R2942000_NEW` slices, and updates every count site.
- New registry test `r2942000_part_three_appends_extended_art_pixel_and_comic`. It checks that:
  - no two of the seven versions take the same cards;
  - each part 3 version has cards no other version takes;
  - each version's cards match the types and rarities its clauses name;
  - Signature fits none of them;
  - `check_pick` and `full_art_picked` refuse them on `core-002` and take them on `classic-056`.
- New API tests:
  - `card_picks.rs`: a version not offered, or Signature beside one, is a 400 and writes nothing; Pixel or Comic with Animated round-trips.
  - `tokens.rs`: an Epic token gets a 400 where the version isn't offered and buys each where it is.
  - `cosmetic_packs.rs`: the Chase Shard bar gives a 400 where the version isn't offered and a 409 (not a chase) where it is, and the bar stays full.
  - `cosmetics.rs`: an existing account owns none of the three.
- `cosmetics.ts` is regenerated.

**Client**
- `versions.ts`: the three ids, and `artPictureOf` returns `"pixel"` and `"comic"`.
- `pictures.ts`:
  - adds `ArtRestyle` and `restyleOf`;
  - adds `pixelSvg` and `comicSvg`, each one SVG filter over the normal picture;
  - adds `restyledSvg`, which picks Sketch, Pixel or Comic.
- `svg.ts` and `CardArt.tsx` replace the Sketch's `sketch` flag with `restyle`. The cache keys for plain pictures and Sketch are unchanged.
- **Extended art**: the normal picture, a delivered art file included, covers the whole face behind a translucent frame and rules box.
  - The frame is the panel itself, faded to nothing toward the middle, so a finish shows through it.
  - A base face's rules box is parchment at 90% over the art. A Radiant face keeps its gold box.
- **Pixel**: 8-bit cells in a retro slate frame. The name is drawn in a built-in 5×7 bitmap face (`pixelName.ts`); the banner's text stays in the DOM, unseen.
- **Comic**: flat colour, halftone dots, ink outlines, and the name in a cyan burst.
- Pixel and Comic set their own frame only on base faces with no border. A worn border keeps its edge and bezel, and Radiant keeps its gold frame.
- zh-CN strings and an ART.md section are added.

**Spec**
- Rulings R2942000 (registry and offers), R2942001 (how each version draws, and Radiant) and R2942002 (augments; Signature on none, through R2949000's existing rule, so no `rulesOut` list).
- `spec/pending/2942.md`, "Amended by" lines on R2725000/1/3/4, and §14.2 and §14.12.
- A `--visual` pending fragment.

## How I tested it
- Rust:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server`: 1703 + 670 + the other binaries ok, with 1 ignored test that was already there.
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test export_cosmetics`: ok, and its only diff is `cosmetics.ts`.
  - `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo jackioh spec check`: "1672 rulings … ok". `patches check` and `catalog check`: ok.
- Web:
  - The harness's command, `vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …`: 323 files, 6076 tests passed.
  - `art/convention.test.ts`, which that command excludes: 10/10.
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint` on the changed files: clean.
  - A mutation check: removing Extended art's full shape fails 24 tests in `versionLooks3.test.tsx`.
- Browser: `cypress run --component --spec cypress/component/card-versions.cy.tsx` passes 10/10 in Electron. The part 3 screenshot is `card-versions-part-3`, and the logged measurements are:
  - Pixel, Comic and Extended art each differ from the normal face (share 0.64 or more against the 0.2 floor).
  - Base Pixel sits in its palette (0.85 against 0.8).
  - Extended art's picture runs past its window (0.73 to 0.79).
- Classify: `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` on the uncommitted tree only reports `Internal`, because HEAD is still `main`. So I wrote the working tree into an unreferenced commit object through a temporary index; no ref, branch or real index changed. `classify --head <that sha> --claims` gave `kind:cards`, `tier:micro`, no problems.

## Decisions the issue left open
- **Subsets**: as planned. Extended art goes on Spells, Pixel on Units and Traps, Comic on action cards, each with a Legendary/Mythic share. Pixel and Comic take no Common card, so Bigot stays bare. The alternative was sharing Full art's cards, which the owner ruled out.
- **Pixel's name face** is a built-in 5×7 bitmap drawn as a background image, rather than a downloaded font; the text stays for screen readers and name lookups. Names with CJK characters print in the normal face.
- **Comic's burst is cyan** because yellow falls in Radiant's gold window.
- **Extended art is not "full art"**: `data-full-art` stays unset and the rules text stays, including in your own hand.
- **No Signature mechanism added**: R2949000 already refuses it, as in part 2.

## Departures from the plan
- **card_picks test card.** The Signature case uses `meditativeplus-026`. `classic-056` isn't offered Signature, so the server refuses it as "not offered" before the R2949000 check runs.
- **Pixel and Comic colour cut.** Each channel now rounds to its nearest level (thresholds at ¼ and ¾) instead of the plan's equal-width bins. With the plan's cut, dark sepia pictures turned black. The output is still the same 27 colours, so the gold-window test still holds.
- **Pixel's sampling.** I changed the plan's 4-unit cell with a 2-unit sample to a 5-unit cell with a 1-unit sample, grown by half a cell over a blurred copy of the picture. Chromium rounds the grow radius down to whole pixels, so at a 120px face the plan's version left gaps between cells or did nothing.
- **Comic's tuning.** I added a small blur and a brightness lift before the cut, moved the halftone dots to the light areas, and lightened, enlarged and spaced the dots. On dark pictures the plan's dots and dense ink edges made the whole picture navy.
- **Extended art's placement.** The picture is a square 150% of the face's height, anchored at the bottom. With plain cover, the subject sat behind the name banner.
- **Rules-box opacity.** 85% parchment failed the watermark contrast floor (R2718000) over black art; 90% passes.
- **New constants.** `EXTENDED_ART_FRAME_OPACITY`, `EXTENDED_ART_BOX_PCT` and `EXTENDED_ART_PICTURE_PCT`, each mirrored in `cards.css` and held to it by tests.

## Worth a second look
- **Rules-box colour test.** I left Extended art's rules box out of the palette test's gold check. It uses `--pal-parchment`, the same parchment as every normal rules box, and that parchment's own hue already falls in the gold window. The test asserts that the box's only colour is that parchment.

# #2942: Patch: Extended art, Pixel and Comic card versions
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

## What it does

This is Part 3 of #2725's ten new card versions (tracker #2729). It adds three Epic restylings of the card's own art:

| Version | What it looks like | Rarity |
|---|---|---|
| **Extended art** (`version-extended-art`) | The card's own art bleeds past its window, behind a translucent rules box and frame (a borderless print) | Epic |
| **Pixel** (`version-pixel`) | The art as 8-bit pixel art in a retro frame, with a pixel face for the name | Epic |
| **Comic** (`version-comic`) | Pop art: halftone dots, heavy ink outlines and flat bright colour, with the name in a burst | Epic |

These sit beside Animated (Epic) in the ladder. Signature never goes on them (#2949).

**Order:** Blocked by #2940 (Part 2: Alt art, Sketch, Alt full art).

## Builds on

#2725 is Part 1 of the plan. It was built in https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/pull/2904. This issue is one of the four parts it left for the ten new versions, split as #2725's plan proposes (**Open questions**, item 1). #2949, which comes first, changes two things this part builds on (the owner's decisions of 2026-11-03): Signature goes only on the Full art version with Animated, with an art and motion of its own, and Full art is offered on a varied set of cards. Read #2725's body first, §1 to §5 and its Acceptance, and rulings R2725000 to R2725004. They give the model this part fills in:

- **What Part 1 built.**
  - A card wears one **version** and the **augments** on it. Both are per-card kinds, owned card by card like a foil.
  - Each entry carries its availability rule as data: `offer`, a list of `OfferClause`s by type, rarity, set, card id and `except`, in `crates/server/cosmetics.json`. It is exported to the client as `COSMETIC_OFFERS`.
  - A card pick is `fullArt` plus `augments`, migration 0079. The server checks every part against ownership and the offer, and answers 400 otherwise. It freezes the pick in the loadout and shows it to the other seat.
  - The client reads `CardLook.version` (`apps/web/src/cards/versions.ts`, `useCardLook` in `fullArt.ts`).
- **What a version from this part adds.** A `version-<slug>` registry entry with its rarity and its `offer`. A painter variant in `apps/web/src/cards/art/`, keyed on `CardLook.version`: a pure function of the card's id, name, tags and type, base and Radiant faces both. The face's frame and CSS where the version restyles them. Its strings in `zh-CN.json`.
- **Which cards get it.** Not every card is offered every version. The owner wants the looks varied across cards (2026-11-03): each version goes to its own subset, not the same cards as Full art or another version, so cards get different mixes. Pick the cards the style suits, give each version a fair spread over every shipped set, and record the rule as data in the entry's `offer`. A version a card isn't offered is never dropped, sold, picked or shown as locked for it.
- **Augments.** Animated and the card's foil, finish and border layer on each new version. **Signature does not** (owner, 2026-11-03): it goes only on the Full art version with Animated, where it has its own art and motion (#2949). Another pairing that cannot work (no layer may be hidden, nothing unreadable, no Radiant mark lost) may be ruled out. Its ruling gives the reason, and the picker and the server both refuse it. If this is the first part to rule one out on a version, it adds that mechanism, for example a `rulesOut` augment list on the entry.
- **Radiant stays easy to tell apart (#2725 §5).**
  - No version uses Radiant's gold on its frame, edge, text marks or stats, and none tints a base face's art gold.
  - On a Radiant face, every version keeps the gold-foil frame (a gold rim on a full-bleed version), R277's marks, the gold stats and the Radiant paint on its picture.
  - Every version keeps the cost gem, the type's panel colour, the crest, the stats, the name (except in hand, #2723) and the rules text at the box's contrast floor.
- **The rest.**
  - Every new entry starts unowned, granted to no account (§14.12). `POST /api/dev/fill` grants it on every offered card.
  - The scale stays Common to Mythic (R2725000).
  - Presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7): no rule reads a version, and nothing enters `PlayerView`'s rules, an action, the log or a replay hash.
  - Its rulings go in this issue's own block, amending R2725000 to R2725004 where it changes them. SPEC §14.2 lists the new versions.
  - It changes how cards look, so it takes a `--visual` pending fragment.

## Acceptance

- The registry holds this part's versions with their rarities, its check passes, and `public.cosmetics` is seeded with them.
- Each version's `offer` is data. A test holds it to at least a named number of cards (config constants, as `VERSION_OFFER_MIN_CARDS` and `_PER_SET`) spread across every shipped set. Another holds every offered (card, version) pair to drawing without error, base and Radiant, and differing from the card's normal face and from every other version.
- A version a card isn't offered is refused with a 400 and writes nothing (pick, token, chase), and the Collection doesn't list it.
- Animated layers on each version unless ruled out, and a foil, finish and border on each. Signature goes on none of them, and the picker and the server refuse it with a 400 (#2949). Every ruled-out pairing is listed in the ruling and refused by the picker and the server.
- Each version's offer is its own: a test holds it different from Full art's and from every other version's.
- Radiant: for each version, with and without its augments, a Radiant face shows Radiant's marks and a base face shows none. The palette test (R2725004's, `RADIANT_GOLD_CLEARANCE`) covers this part's colours.
- A component (pixel) spec shows each version on one Unit and one Spell, base and Radiant, with an augment stack (Animated + a foil) on at least one.
- The rulings pass `cargo jackioh spec check`, and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` passes.
